_meta.purpose: Phase 1 benchmark expansion — categories 3-7 for apple scab + cucurbit powdery mildew, plus a NEW cross-disease category (8) the combined graph enables.
_meta.ground_truth_source: kg_all.ttl / Stage-4 data. Apple scab DE 9 / NO 1; cucurbit mildew DE 1 / NO 1.
_meta.disease_tags: each question carries a 'disease' field so the KG arm routes to the right disease filter.
_meta.note: Powdery mildew leans on negative/absence + cross-border (only 1 product per country); apple scab supports light multi-hop/constraint.
_meta.status: VERIFIED against kg_all.ttl. Key finding: cucurbit mildew shows count-parity (1:1) but SUBSTANCE divergence (DE azoxystrobin vs NO proquinazid).

multi_hop.q: Which active substances are authorised against apple scab in Norway?
multi_hop.answer: dithianon and potassium phosphonate (from Delan Pro).

multi_hop.q: Which active substances are authorised against apple scab in Germany?
multi_hop.answer: captan, dithianon, sulfur, lime sulfur, trifloxystrobin, laminarin, and aureobasidium pullulans (7 substances across 9 products).

constraint.q: Which Norway-authorised apple-scab product contains dithianon?
Which German apple-scab products contain sulfur?
constraint.answer: CURATIO, Microthiol WG, and Thiopron (the sulfur-based products among the 9).

negative.q: Is captan authorised against apple scab in Norway?
negative.answer: No — Norway's only apple-scab product (Delan Pro) contains dithianon + potassium phosphonate, not captan. Definitive absence.

cross_border.q: How does the number of authorised apple-scab products differ between Germany and Norway?
cross_border.answer: Germany 9 vs Norway 1 (Delan Pro). A 9:1 difference.

cross_border.q: Is dithianon authorised against apple scab in both Germany and Norway?
cross_border.answer: Yes — dithianon is authorised against apple scab in both Germany and Norway (confirmed).

negative.q: Is there more than one authorised cucurbit powdery mildew product in Germany?
negative.answer: No — exactly one. A definitive negative.

negative.q: Is sulfur authorised against cucurbit powdery mildew in Norway?
negative.answer: No — Norway's only cucurbit mildew product (Talius) contains proquinazid, not sulfur. Definitive absence.

cross_border.q: For cucurbit powdery mildew, how do Germany and Norway compare in number of authorised products?
cross_border.answer: Both authorise exactly one — Germany 1, Norway 1 (Talius). A rare case of parity.

cross_border.q: Is the active substance in Norway's cucurbit powdery mildew product also authorised in Germany for that disease?
cross_border.answer: No — Norway's product (Talius) contains proquinazid, but Germany's single cucurbit mildew product contains azoxystrobin. Different substances: a genuine cross-border divergence in authorised treatment despite each country having exactly one product.

cross_border.q: Germany and Norway each authorise one cucurbit powdery mildew product — do they use the same active substance?
cross_border.answer: No — Germany uses azoxystrobin, Norway uses proquinazid. Count parity (1 vs 1) but complete divergence in chemistry.

cross_disease._note: NEW category enabled ONLY by the combined graph — document-RAG cannot join a substance across diseases.

questions.q: Which active substances are authorised against more than one of the three diseases (late blight, apple scab, cucurbit powdery mildew)?
questions.answer: azoxystrobin and potassium phosphonate — each authorised against 2 of the 3 diseases.

questions.q: Is azoxystrobin used against only a single disease among the three studied?
questions.answer: No — azoxystrobin is authorised against two of the three diseases. (Tests whether the system can reason across diseases, not just within one.)
